title: Chapter 26 · Amending the Constitution of the Church

current_text.html:
BCO 26-1

The Constitution of the Presbyterian Church in America, which is subject to and subordinate to the Scriptures of the Old and New Testaments, the inerrant Word of God, consists of its doctrinal standards set forth in the Westminster Confession of Faith, together with the Larger and Shorter Catechisms, and the Book of Church Order, comprising the Form of Government, the Rules of Discipline and the Directory for Worship; all as adopted by the Church.

BCO 26-2

Amendments to the Book of Church Order may be made only in the following manner: 1. Approval of the proposed amendment by majority of those present and voting in the General Assembly, and its recommendation to the Presbyteries. 2. The advice and consent of two-thirds (2/3) of the Presbyteries. 3. The approval and enactment by a subsequent General Assembly by a majority of those present and voting.

BCO 26-3

Amendments to the Confession of Faith and the Larger and Shorter Catechisms may be made only in the following manner: 1. Approval of the proposed amendment by three-fourths (3/4) of those present and voting in the General Assembly, and its recommendation to the Presbyteries. 2. The advice and consent of three-fourths (3/4) of the Presbyteries. 3. The approval and enactment by a subsequent General Assembly by three-fourths (3/4) of those present and voting. This paragraph (BCO 26-3) can be amended only by the same method prescribed for the amendment of the Confession of Faith and Catechisms of the church.

BCO 26-4

In voting upon an amendment to the Constitution of the Presbyterian Church in America, the Presbyteries may not divide the parts of the amendment except as directed by the General Assembly which has recommended its adoption.

BCO 26-5

Full organic union and consolidation of the Presbyterian Church in America with any other ecclesiastical body can be effected only in the following manner: 1. The approval of the proposed union by three-fourths (3/4) of those present and voting in the General Assembly and its recommendation to the Presbyteries. 2. The advice and consent of three-fourths (3/4) of the Presbyteries. 3. The approval and consummation by a subsequent General Assembly by three-fourths (3/4) vote of those present and voting. This paragraph (BCO 26-5) can be amended only by the same method prescribed for the amendment of the Confession of Faith and Catechisms of the church.

BCO 26-6

If by reason of the failure of a number of Presbyteries to act, or to report action, on any proposed amendment to the Standards and the response of the Presbyteries is not satisfactory to the succeeding General Assembly, it may defer action for one year. In that event the General Assembly shall urge the delinquent Presbyteries to report their judgment to the next Assembly, which shall take final action on the proposed amendment.

relationships.title: Effect of presbytery division on advice and consent voting
relationships.disposition: Yes to (1), No to (2); Adopted by the CCB

metadata.summary: The CCB advised that a newly erected presbytery may give advice and consent on BCO amendments already voted on by its predecessor, but individual presbyters may not vote a second time after transfer.

occurrences.excerpt: unconstitutionally amend BCO 40-5, contrary to the prescriptions of BCO 26-

metadata.synopsis: A BCO 40-5 citation arose from Metro New York Presbytery's failure to redress a session that allowed a woman to expound Scripture in place of the sermon preceding the Lord's Supper, held services without preaching, and celebrated the Supper without a preceding sermon. The SJC remitted the matter to the presbytery for constitutional resolution because the session's later no-exception response was clearly inadequate and the unapproved minutes were unclear. Presbytery must complete its work with TE Higgins and Trinity Presbyterian Church's session and report to the 51st General Assembly. A separate procedural note questioned the Assembly's direct referral but did not void it.

occurrences.excerpt: …cannot be set aside except by the regular means of amending the constitution (BCO 26). That such is the case is wellfounded in the acts and deliverances of the General Assembly (M29GA, 29- 28, III, pp. 135-136; M21GA (1993) 21-56, III, 18, p. 141-143).

metadata.synopsis: On complaint by RE William F. Mueller, the SJC reviewed whether the Redlands Community Church Session erred on January 14, 2019 by allegedly reaffirming its practice of fencing the Lord's Table contrary to BCO 58-4. The SJC denied the complaint: the only relevant motion failed for lack of a second, so the Session took no action and did not reaffirm anything. It noted the case could have been ruled out of order earlier and that Mueller could pursue relief under BCO 40-5; a concurrence stressed BCO 58-4 remains binding and criticized Presbytery's handling.

relationships.title: Session of Delhi Presbyterian Church v. Louisiana Presbytery

occurrences.excerpt: …of our standards. It is subject to amendment according to the provisions of BCO 26, but not subject to being arbitrarily disregarded by members of the SJC who have vowed to judge all cases according to the Constitution of the Presbyterian Church in…

metadata.synopsis: The SJC sustained a session's timely complaint that Louisiana Presbytery barred one of its members from the Lord's Table after assuming original jurisdiction. Under BCO 33-1, a presbytery may assume jurisdiction only when the session 'refuses to act'; because the session had investigated and found no strong presumption of guilt, it acted, so LAP never acquired jurisdiction. The censure was therefore a nullity, and the member remained under his session. The SJC also held the jurisdictional assumption reviewable despite no timely complaint against it. Three commissioners dissented.

relationships.title: Mt. Carmel Session v. New Jersey Presbytery

occurrences.excerpt: 4. If those who hold that the "24 hour day" view is the only acceptable view for the PCA want to establish that as the official standard for the PCA, the proper approach would be through the formal amendment process in BCO 26.

topics: in the space of six days
presbytery authority to resolve questions of doctrine
metadata.synopsis: Mt. Carmel Session challenged New Jersey Presbytery's creation-days resolution, arguing that the Westminster Standards require six consecutive twenty-four-hour days. The SJC majority concluded that Presbytery could resolve the doctrinal question under BCO 11-4 and that prior Assembly actions permitted latitude on the length of the creation days. The General Assembly rejected the minority report, adopted the majority report, and denied the complaint.
